werk/art-ensemble-of-chicago-message-to-.text:
This album was recorded in Paris on 12 August 1969 for the French label BYG Actuel. The Art Ensemble of Chicago consisted of Lester Bowie on trumpet, Joseph Jarman and Roscoe Mitchell on saxophones and clarinets, and Malachi Favors Maghostut on bass and vocals. Mitchell also played flute, and all four regularly picked up percussion instruments.

The record consists of only four pieces, which vary greatly in length. Old Time Religion lasts just over seven minutes, Dexterity about four, Rock Out just over eight, and A Brain for the Seine, at more than twenty minutes, takes up half the album. Almost all of the music is by Mitchell. It is a record in which short and long pieces alternate.
werk/art-ensemble-of-chicago-message-to-.listen: Listen to A Brain for the Seine, the longest piece, and notice how many different sounds four musicians can make together.

werk/art-ensemble-of-chicago-the-spiritu.text:
The Spiritual is an album by the Art Ensemble of Chicago, recorded in the same sessions as Tutankhamun for the Freedom label. Lester Bowie, Joseph Jarman, Roscoe Mitchell and Malachi Favors Maghostut play here without a drummer. All four therefore also play percussion, and Favors sings as well.

According to a reviewer at AllMusic, the group here seeks out one of the main currents of jazz, the gospel of New Orleans and the music of second line parades, without letting go of the freer sounds. Because there is no regular drummer, there is no rigid tempo binding the musicians together, and that gives them room. The reviewer calls this the artistic peak of the group. The title track lasts more than twenty minutes.
werk/art-ensemble-of-chicago-the-spiritu.listen: Listen to the title track, The Spiritual, and notice how the music holds together without a fixed drum rhythm.

werk/art-pepper-art-pepper-eleven.text:
Art Pepper + Eleven was released in 1960 on Contemporary Records. It is one of the recordings Pepper made in 1959 with the arranger Marty Paich, and the only one on which he is the leader. Paich conducted a small big band and wrote the arrangements for a series of modern jazz classics. They include Move by Denzil Best, Round Midnight by Thelonious Monk and Walkin' Shoes by Gerry Mulligan.

Besides Pepper, who played alto saxophone, tenor saxophone and clarinet, the sessions featured pianist Russ Freeman, bassist Joe Mondragon and drummer Mel Lewis, among others. The clarinet playing in Anthropology is particularly striking.
werk/art-pepper-art-pepper-eleven.listen: Listen to the clarinet in Anthropology and notice how the big band plays around it.

werk/art-pepper-art-pepper-meets-the-rhy.text:
Art Pepper Meets the Rhythm Section is a jazz album from 1957. Pepper plays alto saxophone, together with Red Garland on piano, Paul Chambers on bass and Philly Joe Jones on drums, the celebrated rhythm section of Miles Davis at the time. The record was made on 19 January 1957 at Contemporary's Studios in Los Angeles.

According to Pepper, it became a session under great pressure. He only heard of the recording that morning, did not know the other musicians and admired them all. His instrument was in poor condition and he was struggling with a drug problem. The album is regarded as a milestone in his career. The critic Ben Ratliff wrote that Pepper, unprepared, had to draw the music out of himself. The Penguin Jazz Guide called it a poetic, searing session in which all four men rose above themselves.
werk/art-pepper-art-pepper-meets-the-rhy.listen: Listen to You'd Be so Nice to Come Home To and notice how Pepper's alto saxophone floats over the loose, steady accompaniment of Garland, Chambers and Jones.

werk/art-pepper-surf-ride.text:
Surf Ride is an album by the alto saxophonist Art Pepper with recordings from 1952 to 1954, released as an LP on Savoy in 1956. The tracks come from three sessions in Los Angeles, on 4 March 1952, 29 March 1953 and 25 August 1954. The accompaniment therefore varies. The pianists are Russ Freeman, Hampton Hawes and Claude Williamson, and at the last session Jack Montrose joins on tenor saxophone.

Pepper wrote almost all of the pieces himself, with titles such as Surf Ride, Chili Pepper and Straight Life. Tickle Toe is by Lester Young and The Way You Look Tonight by Dorothy Fields and Jerome Kern. Scott Yanow wrote in AllMusic that the music is brilliant but the packaging leaves something to be desired. The whole is rather arbitrarily assembled, while Pepper is in great form throughout.
werk/art-pepper-surf-ride.listen: Listen to Surf Ride and notice how, in a short track of under three minutes, Pepper sets out his melody straight away.

werk/arthur-blythe-blythe-spirit.text:
Blythe Spirit is the fourth album that the American alto saxophonist Arthur Blythe made for Columbia. It was recorded in New York in 1981. It is a mixture of original compositions and well-known pieces, such as Strike Up the Band by George and Ira Gershwin and Misty by Erroll Garner. There is also a traditional, Just a Closer Walk with Thee.

On most tracks he plays with cello, guitar, tuba and drums, an unusual line-up. On Misty, by contrast, we hear piano and bass, played by John Hicks and Fred Hopkins. On the closing track Amina Claudine Myers plays organ. Scott Yanow of AllMusic calls the record one of the most balanced of his Columbia period, with ties to hard bop, rhythm and blues and the avant-garde. NME placed the album thirtieth on its list of the best records of 1981.
werk/arthur-blythe-blythe-spirit.listen: Listen to Misty and notice how the alto saxophone plays the familiar melody, this time with only piano, bass and drums beneath it.

werk/arthur-blythe-illusions.text:
Illusions is the third album by the alto saxophonist Arthur Blythe for the Columbia label. He recorded it in April and May 1980 at CBS Recording Studios in New York. All of the pieces are his own.

The line-up varies from track to track. In Bush Baby, Illusions and Carespin' with Mamie he plays with cello, guitar and tuba, with James Blood Ulmer on guitar and Abdul Wadud on cello. In Miss Nancy, My Son Ra and As of Yet we hear a more traditional rhythm section of piano, bass and drums, with John Hicks and Fred Hopkins. Robert Palmer placed the album fifth on his list of the best records of 1980 in The New York Times. He wrote that the funk tracks showed that powerful but danceable jazz is not an impossible dream. Scott Yanow of AllMusic calls it recommended.
werk/arthur-blythe-illusions.listen: Listen to Bush Baby and notice the unusual combination of alto saxophone, cello, guitar and tuba, and how together they create a sound of their own.

werk/arthur-blythe-in-the-tradition.text:
In the Tradition appeared in 1963 and is a striking record in the catalogue of Dave Van Ronk. The tracks are divided evenly: half of them he plays with The Red Onion Jazz Band, a combo in the style of Dixieland jazz, and the other half he sings solo, with acoustic guitar.

Both sides suited his personality as a musician. The critic Richie Unterberger of AllMusic found the record somewhat odd for its time, but strong. In his view the sombre acoustic folk blues stand out in particular, and the balanced mix of jazz and folk is the only real difference from the rest of the catalogue. The record is out of print. Part of it appears on the 2002 reissue Two Sides of Dave Van Ronk.
werk/arthur-blythe-in-the-tradition.listen: First listen to Death Letter Blues, with just voice and guitar, and then to See See Rider. Notice how different it sounds when the jazz band joins in.

werk/arthur-blythe-lenox-avenue-breakdow.text:
Lenox Avenue Breakdown was released in 1979 on Columbia Records and reached the Billboard Jazz Albums chart. The line-up is striking: besides the alto saxophonist Arthur Blythe, James Newton plays flute, Bob Stewart tuba, James Blood Ulmer guitar, Cecil McBee bass, Jack DeJohnette drums and Guillermo Franco percussion. Bob Thiele was the producer. According to AllMusic, the group sounds like a band that has played together for years, although the musicians rehearsed for only a week.

The record contains four long tracks, all by the saxophonist himself. Stewart's tuba is a striking voice in the title piece. The album was long unavailable until the 1998 CD. The Penguin Guide to Jazz called it one of the lost masterpieces of modern jazz, and AllMusic ranks it among the three best records in his catalogue.
werk/arthur-blythe-lenox-avenue-breakdow.listen: Listen to Lenox Avenue Breakdown and notice the tuba, which takes a striking leading role in the long solo.

werk/astrud-gilberto-beach-samba.text:
Beach Samba is a studio album by Astrud Gilberto from 1967, with arrangements by Eumir Deodato and Don Sebesky and produced by Creed Taylor. It is included in the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.

The choice of songs is more pop-oriented than on her earlier records for Verve: besides Brazilian songs there are covers such as Misty Roses by Tim Hardin and You Didn't Have to Be So Nice. According to AllMusic it is one of her less impressive albums of the 1960s, although some of the pop choices work well. The reviewer Richie Unterberger particularly praised Não Bate O Coração, in which she scat-sings with confidence and cheek.
werk/astrud-gilberto-beach-samba.listen: Listen to Não Bate O Coração and notice the scat, in which the singer lets loose as she rarely did.

werk/astrud-gilberto-look-to-the-rainbow.text:
Look to the Rainbow is a 1966 album by Astrud Gilberto, with arrangements by Gil Evans and Al Cohn. Evans did most of them, Cohn two tracks on the second side. The eleven tracks are short, often only two to three minutes.

The repertoire combines bossa nova by Antônio Carlos Jobim, João Gilberto and Carlos Lyra with songs such as Once Upon a Summertime, I Will Wait for You and the title track Look to the Rainbow. On Berimbau, Dom Um Romão plays percussion, and I Will Wait for You features a trumpet solo by Johnny Coles.
werk/astrud-gilberto-look-to-the-rainbow.listen: Listen to I Will Wait for You and notice how Johnny Coles's trumpet solo relates to the vocal.

werk/augustus-pablo-ital-dub.text:
Ital Dub was released in 1974. The album came about with Tommy Cowan and Warwick Lyn as producers, instead of Clive Chin, with whom Augustus Pablo had worked before. The role of King Tubby, who mixed the tracks, is striking. He would often do so for Pablo again later.

The album has twelve short tracks, most of about three minutes. Almost all of the pieces were written by Pablo himself, with titles such as The Big Rip Off, Gun Trade and House Raid. Road Block and Curly Dub are also included, with contributors including Bob Marley and Junior Byles. It is a dub record: the space, the echo and the mixing by King Tubby determine the sound here.
werk/augustus-pablo-ital-dub.listen: Listen to Road Block and notice how the mix makes instruments appear and disappear in space.

werk/augustus-pablo-king-tubbys-meets-ro.text:
This 1976 dub record is the work of Augustus Pablo and King Tubby. The sessions with the musicians were recorded at Randy's studio in Kingston, Jamaica. Pablo produced and played melodica, piano, organ and clavinet, with Carlton Barrett on drums, Robbie Shakespeare and Aston Barrett on bass and Earl Chinna Smith on guitar. He then took the tapes to King Tubby, who mixed the tracks. The title track is a dub version of Baby I Love You So by Jacob Miller, which Pablo also produced.

According to Lloyd Bradley, most of the tracks are spectacular remixes of earlier hits or new versions of old Studio One rhythms. Steve Barrow wrote that the record proved that a studio engineer could be as creative as singers, musicians and producers. It later ranked high on lists of the best albums, and according to MusicHound World no earlier dub record had been so influential.
werk/augustus-pablo-king-tubbys-meets-ro.listen: Listen to King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown and notice how the mix makes instruments appear and fall away again, so that the studio itself becomes an instrument.

werk/augustus-pablo-original-rockers.text:
Original Rockers is a compilation album of singles that Augustus Pablo recorded between 1972 and 1975. It was released in 1979 on Greensleeves and compiled by the journalist and photographer Dave Hendley. The tracks were recorded at Channel One and Dynamic Sounds in Kingston, Jamaica, and mixed in the studio of the dub engineer King Tubby.

Robbie Shakespeare and Aston Barrett play bass, Earl Chinna Smith guitar, and Dillinger is guest vocalist on Brace a Boy. The album is included in The Rough Guide to Reggae: 100 Essential CDs. Trouser Press recommended it as a perfect starting point for anyone new to reggae and called the production clear and spirited.
werk/augustus-pablo-original-rockers.listen: Listen to Brace a Boy and notice the voice of Dillinger, the guest vocalist on this track.

werk/augustus-pablo-this-is-augustus-pab.text:
Augustus Pablo released this album in 1974. His childhood friend and reggae producer Clive Chin co-wrote and co-produced it. A whole series of session musicians worked on it, including Ansel Collins on keyboards and Lloyd Parks and Aston Barrett on bass guitar. Carlton Santa Davis, George Fullwood and Earl Chinna Smith are also on the list of musicians.

The album has twelve short instrumental tracks of about three minutes, with titles such as Dub Organizer, Point Blank and Jah Rock. It is one of the first albums on which Pablo's own use of the melodica can be heard, the small keyed wind instrument that would become his trademark. The band plays a rhythmic, spacious reggae sound around it, in which the keyboard work is given plenty of room.
werk/augustus-pablo-this-is-augustus-pab.listen: Listen to Dub Organizer and notice how the melodica and the rhythm section together form one hypnotic whole.

werk/autechre-chiastic-slide.text:
On their fourth album, the British duo Autechre moved further away from the ambient techno of their first records. The beats became harder and full of glitches, the sound colder and more abstract. The album was released in February 1997 on Warp. In the United States it only appeared in 2001, when Warp began distributing there itself. The sleeve was designed by the Sheffield studio The Designers Republic. The fourth track, Cichli, later gave its name to the EP Cichlisuite.

The reception was initially mixed. Some critics found it too repetitive and missed the warm electronic strings of earlier records. Others heard a dark, claustrophobic album full of strange beauty. Appreciation grew later: in 2017 FACT Magazine called it an enduring classic and the pivot around which the work of Autechre turns.
werk/autechre-chiastic-slide.listen: Listen to Cichli and notice the hard, glitchy beats. Hear how little warmth there is compared with ambient techno.

werk/autechre-incunabula.text:
Incunabula was the debut album of the British duo Autechre and was released in late November 1993 on Warp. Rob Brown himself described it as a collection of old material rather than a new album. Eggshell is a reworking of The Egg, a track the duo had previously made for Warp's compilation Artificial Intelligence.

The music is described as techno, ambient techno and IDM: minimal rhythms, bass, keyboard sounds and restrained melodies. According to critics it is more melodic and less experimental than their later work. Bike is regarded as the most song-like moment, while Basscadet combines club rhythms with avant-garde elements. Reviews were mixed: some called it a strong but transitional album, and Fact placed it eleventh on its 2012 list of the best albums of the 1990s.
werk/autechre-incunabula.listen: Listen to Basscadet and notice how a tight dancefloor rhythm is mixed with stranger sounds.

werk/autechre-lp5.text:
Nowhere on the packaging is there a title, which is why this 1998 album by Autechre came to be called LP5. On promotional copies it was called Album, and sometimes it is also simply called Autechre. It was released on Warp. The duo increasingly left behind the warm sounds of earlier records such as Amber. Instead, they chose the technical style of Chiastic Slide and the EP Cichlisuite, supplemented with influences from electroacoustic music.

A track such as Drane2 is a reply in a conversation at a distance: Aphex Twin made a bouncing-ball track in response to Drane, and Autechre answered with the same delay trick, now with percussion in it. Reviews were largely positive. AllMusic called the record uncompromisingly forward-looking. In 2017 Pitchfork placed it eighth on its list of the best IDM albums and spoke of a certain peak.
werk/autechre-lp5.listen: Listen to Drane2 and notice the delay trick with which percussion keeps coming back faster. Hear how that trick is now unleashed on drums.

werk/autechre-tri-repetae.text:
Tri Repetae is the third album by the British duo Autechre and was released in November 1995 on Warp. It sounds different from Incunabula and Amber, the two records that preceded it. The rhythms are more minimal and repetitive, and the melodies lie spaciously and intricately over one another. This shift came out of their time in Sheffield, where they were in close contact with the producers Jez Potter and Mark Fell. Their glitch music inspired the duo to take a new approach. The sleeve, designed by The Designers Republic, shows a plain colour that combines metal and green.

The booklets state that the album sounds best on vinyl, because the surface noise is part of it. Critics responded warmly. Spin compared the duo with Kraftwerk and wrote about emotional electronic music. The record has since been called a turning point for intelligent dance music and is regarded as one of the most influential electronic albums.
werk/autechre-tri-repetae.listen: In Dael or Clipper, listen to how a short rhythmic pattern keeps returning while the sounds around it slowly change. Notice what the machines are doing.

werk/b-j-thomas-reunion.text:
Reunion was released in 1975 on ABC Records and was B. J. Thomas's first country album. Chips Moman produced and played along with the studio musicians, including Reggie Young and Bobby Emmons. Mike Leech wrote the string arrangements.

The record contains the big hit (Hey Won't You Play) Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song, which reached number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and on the easy listening and country singles charts. Crying by Roy Orbison and Sea of Love are also on the album. The album itself reached number 2 on the country chart. The opening track won the award for best country song in 1976.
werk/b-j-thomas-reunion.listen: Listen to (Hey Won't You Play) Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song and notice how the voice tells the story. Hear what the strings add.

werk/backstreet-boys-millennium.text:
Millennium was the long-awaited follow-up to two successful albums from 1997. The group brought a lawsuit against their manager Lou Pearlman, because they felt they were earning next to nothing from their work, and left his management in September 1998. Kevin Richardson lost two relatives, Brian Littrell underwent heart surgery, Howie Dorough lost his sister and the producer Denniz Pop died. The record was first titled Larger than Life. It was released on 18 May 1999.

I Want It That Way, the first single, is regarded as the group's best-known song. Show Me the Meaning of Being Lonely was praised for the way the voices of the five singers blend together. Critics were divided over the record as a whole: some thought it an album of its moment, others found it manufactured and too slick. It became one of the best-selling albums ever, and the accompanying tour was among the fastest-grossing ever.
werk/backstreet-boys-millennium.listen: Listen to Show Me the Meaning of Being Lonely and notice how the five voices alternate and sound together. Who do you hear at which moment?

werk/backstreet-boys-never-gone.text:
Never Gone was released on 14 June 2005 on Jive Records, after a break of almost five years since Black and Blue. In that time each member worked on projects of his own, until the group reunited at the end of 2003. The first recordings with The Underdogs did not catch on. The group then sought out Max Martin again. Unlike on earlier albums, only real instruments can be heard, and the style shifts from teen pop to pop rock.

The title song came about after the death of Kevin Richardson's father. Incomplete was the first single and reached the top ten in several European countries. Critics were mixed to negative: they saw a more mature sound but missed the energy of the earlier hits.
werk/backstreet-boys-never-gone.listen: In Incomplete, listen to how the vocal carries the chorus, with ordinary instruments beneath it instead of synthesizers.

werk/bad-brains-i-against-i.text:
I Against I is the third studio album by Bad Brains and was released on 21 November 1986 on SST Records. It is the best-selling record in their catalogue. The group left their early hardcore punk behind and explored funk, soul, reggae and heavy metal. The title probably refers to the Rastafari expression I and I, which connects the speaker, the audience and Jah. Ron Saint Germain was the producer.

The title track was given a video by Paul Rachman. For Sacred Love, at the producer's suggestion, the vocals were recorded over the telephone from prison, where the singer H.R. was being held for marijuana dealing. The record influenced many rock musicians. Sublime often play House of Suffering as a cover, and other artists name the album as a source of inspiration. Re-Ignition has been sampled several times in hip hop.
werk/bad-brains-i-against-i.listen: Listen to Sacred Love and notice the vocals, which were recorded over the telephone from a prison.

werk/bad-brains-quickness.text:
Quickness is the fourth album by the American band Bad Brains and at the time became their best-selling record. It came after I Against I from 1986, on which reggae had almost disappeared. Here that style returns, alongside funk, hip hop, heavy metal and punk. This produced a crossover that has later also been called one of the first groove metal albums. According to guitarist Dr. Know, the title comes from urgency and speed.

Opener Soul Craft was given an MTV video, directed by Paul Rachman. Drummer Earl Hudson appears on the sleeve but does not play on the record: the drum parts come from Mackie Jayson of the Cro-Mags. Don't Blow Bubbles caused a stir because the lyrics were seen as homophobic. Bassist Darryl Jenifer later called the views he held then ignorant. Critics were divided: one expected more fame, another thought the band was losing its own identity.
werk/bad-brains-quickness.listen: Listen to With the Quickness and try to hear which influences you recognise: does this sound more like punk, metal, funk, hip hop or reggae?

werk/bad-bunny-un-verano-sin-ti.text:
Bad Bunny made this album almost two years after El Último Tour Del Mundo. He announced it with a stadium tour and an advertisement for his Bugatti, in which a phone call played a snippet of Un Ratito. He called it a record to play on the beach in summer, like a playlist.

With twenty-three tracks it is a wide-ranging collection. The basis is reggaeton and cumbia, with indie pop and psychedelia, and many Caribbean styles such as reggae, bomba, dembow, merengue and bachata. Guests include Bomba Estéreo, The Marías and Buscabulla. The sleeve, by the artist Ugly Primo, shows a sad heart in front of a sunny beach. Critics were very positive and praised the versatility. The album reached number one in the United States and was the first record in Spanish to be nominated for a Grammy for Album of the Year.
werk/bad-bunny-un-verano-sin-ti.listen: In Un Ratito, listen to the Caribbean rhythms. Notice how the track fits the idea of an album for the beach.

werk/badfinger-ass.text:
Ass was Badfinger's fifth album and their last on Apple Records. Recording began in January 1972, but the album was not released until 26 November 1973 in the United States and 8 March 1974 in England. Todd Rundgren left the project after two recorded tracks, after which the band tried it themselves. A first version was rejected, and Chris Thomas was given the task, as producer, of improving the recordings.

A dispute over copyright then followed as well, as a result of which Apple credited all the songs to the band. The sleeve, with a donkey behind a carrot, painted by Peter Corriston, refers to the feeling of having been misled by Apple. The album reached number 122 on the Billboard 200.
werk/badfinger-ass.listen: Listen to Apple of My Eye, the opener, and try to hear how this song makes the farewell to the label its subject.

werk/badfinger-straight-up.text:
Straight Up took nine months. First Badfinger recorded an entire record with producer Geoff Emerick, but Apple shelved it. George Harrison took over the work, until he became too busy with the Concert for Bangladesh, at which the group also played. Todd Rundgren then finished the album, in two weeks. The band found his way of working overbearing. Apple also steered the sound, which became less rocking than on earlier records.

Pete Ham wrote the hits Day After Day, Baby Blue and Name of the Game. On Day After Day, Harrison plays slide guitar in a duet with Ham. Critics were mixed when it appeared, but many now regard the album as the group's best. David Fricke of Rolling Stone called it the high point of their power pop.
werk/badfinger-straight-up.listen: Listen to Day After Day and notice the duet of slide guitars between George Harrison and Pete Ham.

werk/bananarama-true-confessions.text:
True Confessions is the third studio album by Bananarama and was released on 30 June 1986 on London Records. Most of it was produced by Tony Swain and Steve Jolley, who had also made the group's first two records. For the first time the group worked with Stock Aitken Waterman, who produced two tracks, including the cover of Venus by Shocking Blue.

The two SAW tracks are dance-oriented. The rest of the album leans towards rock-oriented, serious pop, with lyrics about relationship problems, drugs and a generation that has lost its illusions. There are also two ballads, including the jazzy Dance with a Stranger. Venus became a number 1 on the American Hot 100. Reviews varied: Smash Hits called it a real pop album, while Record Mirror found it no revelation.
werk/bananarama-true-confessions.listen: Listen to Venus and notice how a song from 1969 here becomes a dance track by Stock Aitken Waterman. Hear what the vocals and the beat do.

werk/bananarama-venus.text: On 6 September 1986, Venus by Bananarama was number one in America. It was a new version of a 1969 hit by the Dutch band Shocking Blue. The three singers wanted to turn it into a dance track and approached Stock Aitken Waterman. They hesitated at first, but gave in. The hit factory from south London now had a number one in America as well.
werk/bananarama-venus.listen: Hear how the guitar riff of Shocking Blue has been replaced by a fast synthesizer and a tight drum machine.

werk/bananarama-wow.text:
Wow! is the fourth studio album by Bananarama, released on 7 September 1987 on London Records. It was written and produced entirely with the trio Stock Aitken Waterman, led by Pete Waterman. The sound thereby shifted towards dance-oriented Europop.

The collaboration did not go smoothly. According to Matt Aitken, the group's input in the writing was small, and Siobhan Fahey often clashed with Waterman. Five months after its release she left the group. The album includes I Heard a Rumour, according to one reviewer an example of hi-NRG pop, and a version of the Supremes' Nathan Jones. The album reached number 26 in England and number 1 in Australia. In 2018 Classic Pop named it the second-best record by Stock Aitken Waterman.
werk/bananarama-wow.listen: Listen to I Heard a Rumour and notice the tight, programmed synthesizer groove and the harmonies. Hear how fast and danceable the track is.

werk/barry-white-can-t-get-enough.text:
Can't Get Enough is the third studio album by Barry White and was released on 6 August 1974 on the 20th Century label. He not only wrote the songs and sang them, but also co-arranged them alongside Gene Page, and even came up with the idea for the sleeve, which was painted by Al Harper.

The album became his third number 1 on the R&B chart and also topped the Billboard 200. Two singles reached the top of the R&B chart: Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe and You're the First, the Last, My Everything. Both also did well in the United States and the United Kingdom, and the second became a number 1 there. The critical response was not equally friendly everywhere, since Robert Christgau mainly poked fun at the clichés in the lyrics. Rolling Stone did include the album in its list of the 500 greatest albums.
werk/barry-white-can-t-get-enough.listen: Listen to Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe and notice how the singer's deep voice takes the leading role above the arrangement.

werk/barry-white-i-ve-got-so-much-to-giv.text:
I've Got So Much to Give was released in March 1973 on the 20th Century label and was the singer's debut album. Gene Page did the arrangements together with him. The record already shows what he would stand for: a velvet baritone, surrounded by lush strings. The album topped the R&B chart and reached number 16 on the Billboard 200. Two singles came out of it that reached the R&B top ten: I'm Gonna Love You Just a Little More Baby became number 1 and the title track also did well.

Stephen Erlewine of AllMusic wrote that his sound was already fully formed here and that the closing track was so seductive that it set the tone for the rest of his career. Robert Christgau saw in him a blend of the power of Isaac Hayes and the friendliness of Al Green.
werk/barry-white-i-ve-got-so-much-to-giv.listen: Listen to I'm Gonna Love You Just a Little More Baby and notice how the deep voice and the strings give each other room.

werk/barry-white-is-this-whatcha-wont.text:
Is This Whatcha Wont? is Barry White's sixth album and was released in November 1976 on 20th Century. As on earlier albums, he produced it himself. Gene Page wrote the arrangements and Ray Parker Jr. played guitar on one of the tracks.

The album did less well than its predecessors: it reached number 25 on the R&B chart and thus missed the top ten for the first time. No single reached the R&B top ten either. The two singles were Don't Make Me Wait Too Long and I'm Qualified to Satisfy You. Both also made the English chart. In 1996 a digitally remastered CD edition was released on Mercury Records.
werk/barry-white-is-this-whatcha-wont.listen: Listen to Don't Make Me Wait Too Long and notice how the deep voice and the accompaniment together set the tone.

werk/barry-white-just-another-way-to-say.text:
Just Another Way to Say I Love You is Barry White's fourth album, released in 1975 on 20th Century. White produced it himself. He sang and wrote the arrangements, together with the orchestra leader Gene Page.

The album was a success and reached first place on the R&B chart, his fourth in a row. Two singles came out of it that reached the R&B top ten: What Am I Gonna Do with You became number 1 and I'll Do for You Anything You Want Me To number 4. Both were also hits on the Hot 100 and in England. The album also contains two parts of Love Serenade. In 2006 a digitally remastered CD edition was released.
werk/barry-white-just-another-way-to-say.listen: Listen to Love Serenade (Pt. 1) and notice how the orchestra and the vocal complement each other.

werk/barry-white-stone-gon.text:
Stone Gon' was released in 1973 on 20th Century Records, shortly after the singer's debut. He arranged the record together with Gene Page. Frank Kejmar was the sound engineer, Craig Braun designed the sleeve and Norman Seeff took the photograph.

Like his first, the album topped the R&B chart and reached number 20 on the Billboard 200 and number 18 on the British album chart. Two singles reached the R&B top ten: Never, Never Gonna Give Ya Up and Honey Please, Can't Ya See. Both also did well on the Hot 100, and the first became a hit in England too. In 1994 the record was released on CD, digitally remastered, on Island and Mercury.
werk/barry-white-stone-gon.listen: Listen to Never Never Gonna Give Ya Up and notice how the vocal and the arrangement complement each other.

werk/bauhaus-in-the-flat-field.text:
This debut album by Bauhaus was released on 7 November 1980 on 4AD, the first full-length album on that label. The band had already released three singles, including Bela Lugosi's Dead, and recorded the record themselves at Southern Studios in London. The sound arose under the influence of post-punk bands such as Siouxsie and the Banshees and of David Bowie. The lyrics deal with martyrdom, paranoia, madness and obsession. Dark Entries tells the story of Dorian Gray from the novel by Oscar Wilde.

The British music press fiercely rejected the record on release. Even so, it topped the independent albums chart. Appreciation later grew strongly. One reviewer wrote that the album has almost single-handedly defined the image of gothic rock. Today it is regarded as one of the first and most influential albums of the genre.
werk/bauhaus-in-the-flat-field.listen: Listen to Dark Entries and notice the dramatic vocals of Peter Murphy. The song tells the story of Dorian Gray.

werk/beastie-boys-check-your-head.text:
Check Your Head is the third album by Beastie Boys and was released in April 1992 on Grand Royal and Capitol. After the commercial misfire of Paul's Boutique, which was full of samples, the group returned to its punk roots. In 1991 it recorded the album at G-Son Studios in Atwater Village, under Mario Caldato Jr. For the first time since their early EPs the three played instruments themselves: Adam Horovitz guitar, Adam Yauch bass and Mike Diamond drums. Keyboardist Money Mark took part for the first time.

The record mixes funk and jazz, as in Lighten Up and Something's Got to Give, with hardcore in Time for Livin', a cover of Sly and the Family Stone. The album reached number 10 in America. Reviews varied, from ample praise for the varied, groove-based tracks to fierce disapproval. It later came to be regarded as a touchstone of 1990s alternative rock.
werk/beastie-boys-check-your-head.listen: In Pass the Mic, listen to how the group plays for itself instead of using samples, and notice the loose, playful voices.

werk/beastie-boys-hello-nasty.text:
The Beastie Boys released this fifth album in July 1998, more than four years after Ill Communication. By their own account they spent so long in the studio that they lost touch with the music world. Mix Master Mike, a DMC champion, joined as the new DJ. Guests included Miho Hatori of Cibo Matto on I Don't Know and Lee Scratch Perry on Dr. Lee, Phd. The title is said to come from the receptionist at their New York PR agency, who answered the phone with Hello, Nasty.

According to Pitchfork the record is a love letter to 1980s hip hop, with 808s, disco breaks, beatboxing and scratches, interrupted by dub tracks and ballads. Song for the Man leans towards lounge pop, Song for Junior has a Latin flavour and Flowin' Prose a drum and bass rhythm. Critics were full of praise. Intergalactic won a Grammy for best rap performance by a duo or group.
werk/beastie-boys-hello-nasty.listen: Listen to Song for Junior and notice the Latin-sounding atmosphere. What differs from the hip hop on the rest of the album?

werk/beastie-boys-ill-communication.text:
In 1993 and 1994 the group recorded their fourth album at Tin Pan Alley and G-Son Studios, following the success of Check Your Head. They also founded their own label Grand Royal and published a magazine. Together with Mario Caldato, Jr. they made the record, with Money Mark, Eric Bobo and Amery Smith as guest musicians. Q-Tip and Biz Markie can be heard as guest vocalists. The members listened to the jazz rock of Miles Davis, and the sound relies mainly on live instruments rather than samples.

The record mixes hip hop, punk, jazz and funk. Sabotage began as a fuzz bass track that lay around for a year before vocals were added. The video by Spike Jonze parodied 1970s police series. Sure Shot features a flute sample by Jeremy Steig. Critics were full of praise, and the record reached number one in America and went triple platinum.
werk/beastie-boys-ill-communication.listen: Listen to Sabotage and notice the fuzzy bass that drives the track, and the furious vocals on top of it.

werk/beastie-boys-licensed-to-ill.text:
Licensed to Ill was the debut album of Beastie Boys and was released on 15 November 1986 on Def Jam and Columbia. Producer Rick Rubin was behind the record. It became the first rap album to top the American Billboard 200. It was also the group's only album on Def Jam, because after a dispute with Rubin the group moved to Capitol Records.

The sound mixes rap with hard guitars. Kerry King and Jeff Hanneman of Slayer played guitar, uncredited, on Fight for Your Right and No Sleep Till Brooklyn. The title of the latter track is a nod to the Motörhead album No Sleep 'til Hammersmith, and the video parodies glam metal. On the sleeve, a plane bearing the group's logo has crashed into a mountain. Critics praised the idiosyncratic style and the chemistry between the three rappers. Later lists rank it among the best hip hop and debut albums.
werk/beastie-boys-licensed-to-ill.listen: Listen to No Sleep Till Brooklyn and notice the guitar solo that turns up in the middle of a rap track.

werk/beastie-boys-paul-s-boutique.text:
Paul's Boutique is the second album by Beastie Boys and was released on 25 July 1989 on Capitol Records. After the success of Licensed to Ill the group was written off by many critics, and it left for Los Angeles. Together with the Dust Brothers it made a record with more depth and less commercial material. Recording took two years, including in Matt Dike's apartment. The Dust Brothers already had rhythms and loops ready. The group wanted to keep all of them and rap over the top.

In all, 105 tracks were sampled from funk, soul, rock and jazz, 24 fragments on the final track alone. For the sleeve the group hung a sign reading Paul's Boutique on an existing shop in Manhattan. The record sold less than the debut, but received unanimously positive reviews. It is now regarded as a milestone of the golden age of hip hop, and is sometimes called the Sgt. Pepper of hip hop.
werk/beastie-boys-paul-s-boutique.listen: Listen to B-Boy Bouillabaisse, the long closing piece, and notice how many different fragments pass by one after another.

werk/beastie-boys-to-the-5-boroughs.text:
This sixth record was released on 14 June 2004, the group's first major release since Hello Nasty in 1998. The album looks back at New York after the attacks of 11 September. The first single, Ch-Check It Out, could already be heard in the series The O.C. before the record came out. Triple Trouble, Right Right Now Now and An Open Letter to NYC followed.

The group samples a lot of old hip hop. Rhyme the Rhyme Well features the voice of Chuck D of Public Enemy and That's It That's All a sample of Rock Box by Run-DMC. Reviewers appreciated the simple beats without the frills that, according to one critic, made Hello Nasty distracting. Rolling Stone called the album fast, funny and sobering, and PopMatters the best record since Paul's Boutique. It was nominated for a Grammy for best rap album.
werk/beastie-boys-to-the-5-boroughs.listen: Listen to Rhyme the Rhyme Well and notice the voice of Chuck D, which is sampled in the track.

werk/bee-gees-bee-gees-1st.text:
Bee Gees’ 1st is the group's third studio album, but the first to be released internationally, after two records that came out only in Australia and New Zealand. It was released on 14 July 1967 in the United Kingdom. Recording began on 7 March, shortly after the Gibb brothers' return to England, at IBC Studios. Drummer Colin Petersen and guitarist Vince Melouney, both Australians, were brought in to make them into a proper band. The sleeve is by Klaus Voormann, who also designed the Beatles' Revolver.

It is psychedelic rock and pop. To Love Somebody, New York Mining Disaster 1941 and Holiday were hits and give the record a melancholy tone. Every Christian Lion Hearted Man Will Show You opens with Gregorian-style chanting and mellotron. According to the critic Bruce Eder, it was more of a rock album than the group had been given credit for. By the end of 1967 it was in the top ten in three countries.
werk/bee-gees-bee-gees-1st.listen: Listen to Every Christian Lion Hearted Man Will Show You and notice the Gregorian-style chanting and the mellotron with which the song begins, before the psychedelic pop song breaks loose.

werk/bee-gees-horizontal.text:
Horizontal is the fourth studio album by the Bee Gees and the second to be released internationally, in early 1968. The first session took place on 17 July 1967, three days after Bee Gees’ 1st came out, at Central Sound on Denmark Street in London. According to the group, the point now was that the three brothers wanted to do things their own way and to experiment with sounds and arrangements. Bill Shepherd's orchestra is a fixed part of those arrangements. The influences range from the Beatles to baroque pop, and The Change Is Made comes from their love of R&B.

Massachusetts and World became international hits. World is a sombre ballad with mellotron, a dense piano sound and a fuzz guitar. The record sounds darker and heavier than its predecessor, partly owing to the greater input of guitarist Vince Melouney and drummer Colin Petersen. Fans responded with mixed feelings. The album reached the top twenty worldwide.
werk/bee-gees-horizontal.listen: Listen to World and notice the trembling mellotron and the fuzz guitar that together colour the sombre ballad.

werk/ben-webster-ben-webster-and-associa.text:
In 1959 the tenor saxophonist Ben Webster recorded a session for the Verve label that was entirely about the space of the long-playing record. He played together with Coleman Hawkins and Budd Johnson, also both on tenor saxophone, and with the trumpeter Roy Eldridge. The rhythm section consisted of Les Spann on guitar, Jimmy Jones on piano, Ray Brown on bass and Jo Jones on drums.

The centrepiece of the record is In a Mellow Tone by Duke Ellington and Milt Gabler. The piece lasts twenty minutes and fills the whole first side. The soloists do not fight for first place, but jam in a relaxed way, like friends among themselves. The session also became a tribute to Lester Young, a tenor saxophonist of the same generation, who had died less than four weeks earlier. The website Allmusic gave the album four and a half stars.
werk/ben-webster-ben-webster-and-associa.listen: Listen to In a Mellow Tone and notice how the four soloists give each other room, without it becoming a contest.

werk/ben-webster-ben-webster-meets-oscar.text:
On 6 November 1959 the tenor saxophonist Ben Webster recorded this studio album, accompanied by the trio of the pianist Oscar Peterson. Bassist Ray Brown and drummer Ed Thigpen formed the rhythm section. A year later the record was released on Verve.

The repertoire consists of standards, such as The Touch of Your Lips, Bye Bye Blackbird and How Deep Is the Ocean?. At almost ten minutes, This Can't Be Love is the longest track. According to Stephen Cook of Allmusic, Peterson gets more than enough solo time, and yet he discreetly shadows the saxophonist's airy tone and supple phrasing. Cook called it an excellent first introduction to the saxophonist and one of his very best records.
werk/ben-webster-ben-webster-meets-oscar.listen: Listen to This Can't Be Love and notice how the piano follows the saxophone without drowning it out.

werk/ben-webster-king-of-the-tenors.text:
King of the Tenors contains recordings from 1953 for the Norgran label. The album first appeared as The Consummate Artistry of Ben Webster and was released in 1957 on Verve under the title it has had ever since. Webster plays tenor saxophone, accompanied by the Oscar Peterson Trio. On a number of tracks Benny Carter on alto saxophone and Harry Edison on trumpet also take part.

According to the biographer Frank Buchmann-Moller, the record shows a broad range of Webster's abilities. On the blues numbers Jive at Six and Bounce Blues he plays with fire, and Cottontail is built over six choruses. The ballads stand out most, beginning with Tenderly. In Don't Get Around Much Anymore he plays the theme almost seductively. The Penguin Guide to Jazz gave the album its highest rating.
werk/ben-webster-king-of-the-tenors.listen: Listen to Tenderly and notice the warm, soft tone of the tenor saxophone in the ballad.

werk/benny-carter-aspects.text:
In the late summer of 1958 the saxophonist and arranger Benny Carter recorded this album. United Artists released it a year later, sometimes also under the title The Jazz Calendar of Benny Carter. The idea is as simple as it is playful: each track belongs to a month of the year, from June in January to Roses in December. Carter used two overlapping big bands, which he arranged himself and in which he played alto saxophone.

According to AllMusic it is his only big band recording as a bandleader between 1947 and 1986. The music is solid mainstream swing, sounding by turns powerful and lyrical. The reviewer called some of the titles somewhat contrived, but the quality of the playing is not included in that. The album shows how Carter, who was originally associated with big bands, once again led a large band.
werk/benny-carter-aspects.listen: Listen to September Song and notice how the big band carries the familiar theme and how Carter's arranging gives the old song a new colour.

werk/benny-carter-cosmopolite.text:
Cosmopolite is an album by the saxophonist Benny Carter, recorded in three sessions between 1952 and 1954 and released by Norgran Records. Some of the tracks had previously appeared on the 10-inch LP The Urbane Mr. Carter.

The album presents the alto saxophonist in two very different settings. On the first side he plays ballads in front of a string group. On the other side he stands alongside the trio of the pianist Oscar Peterson and the drummer J.C. Heard. AllMusic gave the album three stars and called it proof of his versatility: he plays exceptionally well in both formats.
werk/benny-carter-cosmopolite.listen: Listen to I Get a Kick Out of You and notice how the alto saxophone sings the theme while the rest of the group plays calmly around it.

werk/benny-carter-jazz-giant.text:
Jazz Giant was recorded in 1957 and 1958 and released on Contemporary Records. It is a session with a septet, in which Benny Carter plays alto saxophone and trumpet and also wrote the arrangements. He plays together with, among others, the tenor saxophonist Ben Webster, the trombonist Frank Rosolino, the pianist André Previn, the guitarist Barney Kessel, the bassist Leroy Vinnegar and the drummer Shelly Manne.

According to AllMusic, the music does not fit a pigeonhole such as swing or bop and simply deserves the name classic. The Penguin Guide to Jazz called it a great record for a small group, full of imagination and ingenuity, with classic interplay between the bandleader and Webster.
werk/benny-carter-jazz-giant.listen: Listen to Old Fashioned Love and notice how the soloists complement and answer one another in the ensemble playing.

werk/benny-golson-benny-golson-s-new-yor.text:
This is the debut album of the saxophonist Benny Golson. The recordings date from late 1957 and the album was released on the Contemporary label. Golson played tenor saxophone and the trumpeter Art Farmer was his regular foil. Pianist Wynton Kelly, bassist Paul Chambers and drummer Charlie Persip formed the rhythm section. On three tracks the quintet became a nonet, with Jimmy Cleveland on trombone, Julius Watkins on horn, Gigi Gryce on alto saxophone and Sahib Shihab on baritone saxophone.

The record includes Whisper Not and Step Lightly, among others. Something in B flat is by Ray Bryant and Capri by Gigi Gryce. A reviewer at the time wrote that Farmer played with broad authority throughout and that Golson's warm, dark lines glide through all the pieces. Scott Yanow later called the record an underrated gem and a strong start to an influential solo career.
werk/benny-golson-benny-golson-s-new-yor.listen: Listen to Whisper Not and notice the warm, dark tone of Golson's tenor saxophone, as critics described it.

werk/benny-golson-groovin-with-golson.text:
Groovin' with Golson is the sixth album by the saxophonist Benny Golson. The recordings date from 1959 and the record was released on the New Jazz label. Golson plays tenor saxophone in a quintet with the trombonist Curtis Fuller, the pianist Ray Bryant, the bassist Paul Chambers and the drummer Art Blakey.

There are five tracks, two of them by Golson himself: My Blues House and The Stroller, both lasting almost nine and a half minutes. The group also plays Drum Boogie by Roy Eldridge and Gene Krupa and two standards, I Didn't Know What Time It Was by Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart and Yesterdays by Jerome Kern and Otto Harbach. Scott Yanow wrote in AllMusic that the hard bop on this record does indeed groove in its own way.
werk/benny-golson-groovin-with-golson.listen: Listen to My Blues House and notice how the saxophone and the trombone take turns and how the band keeps swinging underneath.

werk/benny-golson-the-other-side-of-benn.text:
The Other Side of Benny Golson is the saxophonist's third album as a bandleader. It was recorded in late 1958 and originally released on the Riverside label. He plays tenor saxophone in a quintet with the trombonist Curtis Fuller, the pianist Barry Harris, the bassist Jymie Merritt and the drummer Philly Joe Jones.

The album was important for two reasons. It was the first time he worked with Fuller; in 1960 they would play together in The Jazztet. He was also given one of his first chances here to play at length as a soloist, since previously he had mainly been known as a composer. Most of the tracks are his own, with exceptions such as Jubilation by Junior Mance, Symptoms by Fuller and This Night by Richard Evans.
werk/benny-golson-the-other-side-of-benn.listen: Listen to Strut Time and notice how the tenor saxophone and trombone are given room in the solos.

werk/benny-green-the-place-to-be.text:
The pianist Benny Green recorded The Place to Be in 1994 for the Blue Note label. He played with his trio, with Christian McBride on bass and Kenny Washington on drums. On three tracks a horn section joins the trio, with arrangements by Bob Belden: Nice Pants, I Want to Talk About You and I Felt That. A tuba and a horn are thus also part of the line-up.

The record mixes original compositions with standards and lesser-known pieces by, among others, Billy Eckstine, Clare Fischer, Freddie Hubbard and Oscar Peterson. Scott Yanow of AllMusic heard in this playing the influence of Peterson and other predecessors, but also a musical voice of his own. William Grimm wrote on All About Jazz that he is an accomplished jazz pianist who commands the older styles, from stride to bebop.
werk/benny-green-the-place-to-be.listen: In Nice Pants, listen to how the horns and the piano trio build the piece together, and notice when the piano carries on without the horns.

werk/beyonce-4.text:
After her third album, Beyoncé took a break from her career in 2010. She severed the business tie with her father and manager Mathew Knowles and in March 2010 began new recordings in New York. The sessions ran until May 2011 and took place in many locations, including Peter Gabriel's Real World Studios. She wanted to make a calmer album, rooted in old-fashioned rhythm and blues, with live instruments, horns and real songs.

The sound leans on 1970s funk, 1980s pop and 1990s soul. In End of Time there are horns and percussion inspired by Fela Kuti. Love On Top later won a Grammy. Reviews were generally positive and the album reached first place on the Billboard 200 in the United States.
werk/beyonce-4.listen: Listen to End of Time. Notice the horns and the percussion parts, which sound like a marching band.

werk/beyonce-b-day.text:
Beyoncé's second solo album was actually planned for before 2004, but was shelved because of Destiny's Child's last record and the film Dreamgirls. Only after filming did she go into the studio. In April 2006 she hired Sony Music Studios in New York and had several producers work at the same time in separate rooms, including Rodney Jerkins, The Neptunes, Stargate and Swizz Beatz. She walked from room to room, and the album was recorded in about two weeks.

The role in Dreamgirls inspired many of the lyrics. Musically the record ranges from 1970s and 1980s funk to ballads and hip hop, pop and R&B, and real instruments can be heard on most tracks. Déjà Vu was the first single, and Irreplaceable became a number one in the United States. Reviews were mostly favourable, especially about the sound and the vocals. The album won a Grammy for Best Contemporary R&B Album.
werk/beyonce-b-day.listen: In Ring The Alarm, listen to the way the vocals ride over the tight beat. Notice how much energy there is in her voice.

werk/beyonce-beyonce.text:
On 13 December 2013 this fifth album by Beyoncé appeared as a surprise, as a visual album with a video for each track. Everything had been recorded in secret. In 2012 she had had producers and writers stay at her house in the Hamptons for a month. After a break for tours she continued in 2013 and looked for styles outside conventional R&B. The plan was an album in a month and a half, but it took a year and a half.

The result is electro-R&B with heavy bass, percussion and synthesizers, and with dark, personal lyrics about sexuality and monogamy. Drunk in Love with Jay-Z reached number 2 on the American Hot 100 and won two Grammys. The album broke the record for the fastest-selling album in the iTunes Store and received glowing reviews. The surprise release led the IFPI to move the worldwide release day from Tuesday to Friday.
werk/beyonce-beyonce.listen: Listen to Drunk in Love and notice the heavy, dreamy production and how the vocals and Jay-Z's rap alternate.

werk/beyonce-cowboy-carter.text:
Beyoncé grew up in Houston, where country and rodeo were part of her childhood. Her country track Daddy Lessons from 2016 drew criticism from people who felt she did not belong in the genre. That led her to research the history of country music, and in doing so she discovered its Black roots. She began Cowboy Carter in 2019, recorded it during the pandemic and made it the second part of a trilogy. It came out after Renaissance, although it had originally been planned earlier.

The album is a wide-ranging mix of music from the American South, performed with acoustic instruments. It sounds like a radio broadcast with Dolly Parton, Linda Martell and Willie Nelson as DJs. Texas Hold 'Em became the first country song by a Black woman to top the Billboard Hot 100. Critics praised the ambitious reworking of Americana. The album won the Grammy for Album of the Year.
werk/beyonce-cowboy-carter.listen: In SMOKE HOUR ★ WILLIE NELSON, listen to the voice of Willie Nelson. Notice how he sounds like a DJ presenting the album as a radio broadcast.

werk/beyonce-dangerously-in-love.text:
During the recording of Survivor, Destiny's Child's third album, it was decided that each member would make a solo record. From March 2002 to March 2003 Beyoncé worked on her debut in various studios, while the group lay dormant. She chose the producers herself, started in Miami with Scott Storch and took her time, unlike with the rushed group albums. As executive producer she co-wrote the majority of the songs. Guests included Jay-Z, Missy Elliott, Sean Paul, Big Boi and Luther Vandross.

The music is mainly R&B, with elements of soul, hip hop and Arabic music, and alternates fast tracks with ballads. Crazy in Love and Baby Boy spent eight and nine weeks respectively at number one on the American Hot 100. Reviews were mixed, but the album became a great commercial success and won five Grammys, including Best Contemporary R&B Album.
werk/beyonce-dangerously-in-love.listen: Listen to Crazy in Love and notice how the vocals and Jay-Z's guest appearance respond to each other.

werk/beyonce-i-am-sasha-fierce.text:
Beyoncé recorded this third solo album between November 2007 and August 2008, with Stargate, The-Dream, Ryan Tedder and Babyface, among others. It was originally a double album meant to show two sides of her. The first disc, I Am..., contains quiet pop and R&B ballads with influences from folk and alternative rock, and she used instruments she was not used to, such as acoustic guitar. The second disc is named after her stage alter ego Sasha Fierce and contains faster tracks with electropop and Europop.

If I Were a Boy and Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It) became the best-known singles, and Single Ladies reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100. Reviews ranged from mixed to positive, but the album reached number one on the American album chart. At the Grammy Awards it received seven nominations, including Album of the Year, and won five.
werk/beyonce-i-am-sasha-fierce.listen: In If I Were a Boy, listen to the acoustic guitar beneath the vocals. Then compare that with the tempo of Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It).

werk/beyonce-renaissance.text:
Renaissance was released in 1987 and is an album by the saxophonist Branford Marsalis. His brother Delfeayo produced it. Marsalis plays tenor and soprano saxophone, Tony Williams drums and Bob Hurst bass. St. Thomas, a piece by Sonny Rollins, he plays solo. Herbie Hancock plays piano on The Peacocks, written by Jimmy Rowles. Lament is by J. J. Johnson.

Reviewers called it an acoustic jazz album in the tradition. The Washington Post praised the arrangement of The Peacocks, in which Marsalis's supple soprano and Hancock's sounds come together. Other newspapers praised his melodic, relaxed approach and the supple solos.
werk/beyonce-renaissance.listen: Listen to St. Thomas and notice how the saxophone manages without accompaniment. Hear how the melody carries everything.
